security_audit.summary: The skill is primarily a markdown guide, and most command findings are false positives from fenced examples rather than runnable shell-backtick code. The quick start includes a confirmed critical curl-to-shell installer pattern, and the remote image URL is a low-risk external content fetch. No prompt injection attempt or hidden data-exfiltration instruction was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Quick start pipes a remote installer directly into a shell.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-shell command with manual download, checksum verification, and an explicit install command users can inspect first.

remediation.issue: Marketplace content references a remotely hosted image.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle a local image asset or proxy the image through trusted marketplace infrastructure to avoid third-party fetches.

remediation.issue: Examples submit prompts and sample data to external AI providers through the inference.sh CLI.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear privacy note reminding users to remove secrets, private code, and customer data before sending prompts externally.

content.user_title: Improve AI Prompts for Text, Images, and Video
content.value_statement: AI results often fail when prompts are vague or poorly structured. This skill provides reusable patterns for LLM, image, and video prompts.
actual_capabilities: Explains role, task, constraint, and output format prompt structure.
Shows few-shot, chain-of-thought, and structured output examples.
Provides prompt patterns for LLM, image, and video generation.
Includes model-specific tips for Claude, GPT-4, FLUX, and Veo.
Offers reusable templates for code review, content writing, and image generation.
limitations: Does not evaluate prompt quality automatically.
Requires user review before submitting sensitive data to external models.
Uses inference.sh CLI examples that may require account setup.
Does not guarantee identical results across models or providers.

use_cases.title: Create Reliable Work Prompts
use_cases.description: Turn vague requests into structured prompts with roles, constraints, and expected formats.

use_cases.title: Improve Code Review Requests
use_cases.description: Ask AI tools to review code for bugs, security issues, performance, and style.

use_cases.title: Draft Media Generation Prompts
use_cases.description: Build prompts for image and video models with subject, style, composition, lighting, and motion details.

prompt_templates.title: Clarify a Basic Prompt
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this prompt using role, task, constraints, and output format: [draft prompt]. Keep it direct and testable.

prompt_templates.title: Create Few-Shot Examples
prompt_templates.scenario: Teaching a model a repeatable pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Build three examples that teach the model how to complete this task: [task]. Include input, expected output, and one edge case.

prompt_templates.title: Specify Structured Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a prompt that extracts [information type] from [source text]. Define the fields, allowed values, and validation rules in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multi-Step Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a three-turn prompting workflow for [business problem]. First diagnose causes, then prioritize options, then propose validation tests.

output_examples.input: Vague request: Help me write a product update.
output_examples.output: A clearer prompt that defines the audience, tone, required points, length, and acceptance criteria.

output_examples.input: Need an image prompt for a mountain lodge.
output_examples.output: A detailed image prompt with subject, setting, lighting, composition, style, and quality terms.

output_examples.input: Need to analyze why shoppers abandon checkout.
output_examples.output: A three-step prompt sequence that identifies causes, ranks fixes, and proposes validation tests.

best_practices: State the role, task, constraints, and expected format before examples.
Use representative examples and include edge cases when accuracy matters.
Review prompts for sensitive data before using external model providers.
anti_patterns: Asking broad questions without success criteria or output format.
Mixing conflicting style, length, or audience requirements.
Using private code, customer data, or credentials in third-party prompts.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps you write clearer prompts for text models, image generators, and video models.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is general and can be adapted for Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and similar tools.

faq.question: Does it require the inference.sh CLI?
faq.answer: The examples use inference.sh commands, but the prompt patterns can be used without the CLI.

faq.question: Can it create prompts for images and video?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers subject details, style, composition, lighting, camera movement, and negative prompts.

faq.question: Will it guarantee the same output every time?
faq.answer: No. Model settings, provider behavior, and prompt wording can still change results.

faq.question: Should I include private data in prompts?
faq.answer: No. Remove secrets, credentials, private code, and personal data before sending prompts to external providers.
